extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff, environmental regulators, legal counsel, and the informed public interested in vehicle emissions enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a congressional oversight hearing focusing on the EPA's Notice of Violation to Volkswagen for use of defeat devices, the agencies' investigative and enforcement approach, testing and recall requirements, and impacts on consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Conformity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All new cars sold in the United States must have an EPA-issued Certificate of Conformity demonstrating that the car meets applicable Federal emissions standards to control air pollution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vehicles certified to EPA standards must match produced-on-road emissions; selling vehicles with features that defeat certified performance violates the certification requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and prohibition of a 'defeat device'
rubrics_metrics.description: Software that senses when the vehicle is being tested for compliance and turns off or significantly reduces the effectiveness of emissions controls during normal driving while turning them on during official emissions tests is a 'defeat device.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a design feature is unlawful; EPA characterized VW's software as a defeat device that allowed on-road NOx emissions up to 40 times allowable levels. Inputs used to detect testing can include steering wheel position, vehicle speed, engine operation duration, and barometric pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Violation (NOV) scope and allegation framing
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA issued an NOV alleging that certain Volkswagen and Audi diesel cars (roughly 482,000 vehicles, model years 2009–2015) include software that circumvents EPA's emissions standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOVs trigger investigations to assess statutory violations and potential remedies; they define the initial scope of enforcement and the vehicles/models implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seriousness of violation and concealment as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Making and selling vehicles with defeat devices that allow higher emissions than certified violates multiple Clean Air Act provisions, and concealment of such facts from EPA, California, and consumers is particularly serious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concealment may increase enforcement severity and influence penalty and remedy determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation objectives and elements to assess
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA intends to assess the scope of VW's liability under the Clean Air Act, whether there are additional vehicles with defeat devices, the economic benefit to VW of noncompliance, appropriate penalties, the excess pollution from violations, and appropriate mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations will consider civil penalties, remedial actions (recalls/fixes/buybacks), pollution mitigation, and economic disgorgement; EPA coordinates with DOJ and CARB and may withhold details to avoid jeopardizing the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for manufacturers to provide documentation and explanation for recalls
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee requested documents showing what Volkswagen told consumers and regulators about the December 2014 voluntary recall and the reasons given for that recall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers should preserve and produce recall-related communications and technical justification for both consumers and regulators; transparency to oversight bodies is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer responsibility to identify causes and propose effective fixes
rubrics_metrics.description: It is VW's responsibility to identify what was wrong with the vehicles and to propose a fix; proposed fixes must be tested and shown to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators (CARB/EPA) will evaluate manufacturer-proposed remedies and will require additional testing if fixes are ineffective (e.g., December 2014 software fixes were later shown by CARB not to be effective).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to present multiple remedy options
rubrics_metrics.description: California and EPA have directed Volkswagen to present more than one option on how to address the excess emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators will review alternative fixes carefully, particularly with respect to impacts on vehicle owners (fuel economy, performance, physical modifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of owner/consumer impacts in remedy review
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating proposed solutions, EPA and CARB will look carefully at impacts on owners (e.g., fuel economy, engine performance, need for structural changes such as urea systems, trunk-space impacts, resale value).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies that negatively affect consumers may be scrutinized; consumer make-whole considerations are part of enforcement and remedy design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variability of fix feasibility by engine generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility and complexity of fixes depend on engine generation: newer (Generation 3) engines are believed easier to fix, while older generations (2009–2014) lacking urea systems may require more substantial engineering, possibly installation of urea systems or different NOx filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators will require appropriate engineering solutions per vehicle generation and will consider feasibility, cost, and owner impacts when approving remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing regime adjustments: unpredictability and mixed methods
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will adjust testing going forward to be unpredictable and will use a robust mix of lab testing of new vehicles, lab testing of in-use vehicles, and on-road measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpredictable and mixed-method testing reduces the effectiveness of calibration strategies designed to pass only standardized tests; manufacturers should expect increased and varied verification testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to assess and mitigate excess pollution
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of enforcement, EPA intends to assess the excess pollution resulting from VW's violations and identify appropriate ways to mitigate those emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation may be part of remedy packages alongside penalties and fixes; assessment quantifies public-health impacts to inform remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement authority and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's Civil Enforcement Program develops and prosecutes civil administrative and judicial cases; EPA will work closely with the U.S. Department of Justice and the California Air Resources Board during the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil enforcement is coordinated across agencies; DOJ involvement may shape litigation strategy and penalty recovery; EPA may defer public disclosure of investigative details to protect enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of economic benefit of noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA intends to assess the economic benefit to Volkswagen from noncompliance (i.e., the advantage gained by selling noncompliant vehicles) as part of determining appropriate penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifying economic benefit can increase penalty amounts and inform disgorgement or other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Product Safety/Technical Engineering in recall development
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary recalls and proposed fixes were developed by VW's Technical Engineering Department in conjunction with the Product Safety Committee worldwide, which steers recall campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators will examine who developed and approved fixes internally when assessing corporate responsibility and oversight failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer information and safety messaging during investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has provided FAQs for consumers (e.g., whether cars are safe to drive, whether EPA is officially recalling vehicles) and recognizes an obligation to consider consumer impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear public messaging helps protect consumer safety and informs owners about recall and repair processes; regulators expect manufacturers to communicate transparently with consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency expectation for prompt and testable proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA and CARB pressed VW for urgent proposals and expect to receive concrete plans (e.g., EPA hoped to see a proposal soon for Generation 2 vehicles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators expect timely submissions accompanied by data and software for independent verification and testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: State inspection and registration implications for owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether owners face penalties or registration barriers depends on state-level emissions inspection regimes; some states require proof that a recall fix has been made to re-register a vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners must follow state inspection requirements; EPA indicated it does not anticipate prosecuting individual owners under the Clean Air Act for driving affected vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement resourcing and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's enforcement will continue along normal investigative paths, but agencies expect an increase in public tips/calls and will scale responses accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement offices should be prepared for increased public engagement and case workload arising from high-profile compliance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory oversight rationale: level playing field and consumer protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight ensures the benefits of clean-air emissions standards are realized, that industry competes on a level playing field, and that consumers get what they pay for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators justify strict enforcement to maintain public-health protections and fair market conditions; remedial actions aim to restore these equities.
